dedupe_keys.name: infraflood nc infrastructure specific flood extent annotations for roads and buildings in north carolina hurricanes matthew and florence

description: InfraFlood-NC provides binary flood extent annotations for individual infrastructure assets in six urban areas of North Carolina severely affected by Hurricanes Matthew and Florence. Flood masks from the very high-resolution DeepFlood imagery dataset (1.5 to 25 cm) were reclassified into wet and dry, paired with vector road networks and building footprints, and zonal statistics give the maximum inundation presence per structure; critical facility classes were joined from the Homeland Infrastructure Foundation-Level Data. It was produced by Timothy Agboada, Leila Hashemi-Beni and Jeffrey Blay and published on figshare in March 2026. Coverage is local, in ten spatial divisions of six urban areas. The data are free under CC BY 4.0 and available to download as GeoJSON for training visual question answering models and as shapefiles for GIS risk assessment, such as buffered road layers. Caveats: it records flooded or not, not depth, for two events only, and depends on the quality of the DeepFlood labels. It supports flood exposure of road segments and validation of flood damage and network disruption models. It complements the FHWA emergency relief resilience case studies and is related to the RA2CE road network resilience toolkit.
